text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - British shares rose on Tuesday, with the leading FTSE 100 index closing 33 points off its record peak, even as the British Government unloaded 257 million stg worth of utility shares into the market. Buoyed by firm debt and stock index futures markets plus a rebound on Wall Street, the benchmark blue chip FTSE 100 index settled 23.0 points higher at 4,061.5.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index of leading shares stormed higher on Tuesday and ended bourse dealings at its fourth record close in a row, after the dollar soared to a 23-month high against the mark. Strength in German government bonds, also at record highs, provided additional support for the market. The DAX 30-share index closed floor trade at 2,886.98 points, marking a gain of 28.38 points, or 0.99 percent. Later the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index stood at 2900.76 up 47.30 points.

PARIS - French stocks closed more than one percent higher on Tuesday, setting a new high for the year, but fell short of matching their all-time high. Traders said the bourse was lifted by a stronger dollar and growing expectations of near-term interest rate cuts in Europe. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed 30.48 points or 1.31 percent higher at 2,349.11 -- within reach of its historic record of 2,360.98 set in February 1994.

ZURICH - Swiss shares staged a record-breaking run, ending at new all-time highs in both the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) and the broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI). Dealers said the market may continue to break new ground. "We may see 4,000 SMI points in the next few days", one said. The Blue-chip SMI was up 1.29 percent, or 50.1 points, to 3,924.1. The Broad SPI added 25.35 points, or 1.02 percent, to 2,504.14.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed slightly lower on Tuesday after a day of volatile trade. The Nikkei average's decline, which continued from Monday, induced some buying back in late trade, but the bottom side is likely to be still vulnerable. The key Nikkei 225 average was down 44.13 points, or 0.21 percent, at 20,630.56. Its December futures were 20 points lower at 20,660.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended down on Tuesday as investors took a more defensive stance following recent gains, but finished off the day's lows as some buyers continued to cautiously pick up laggards. The Hang Seng Index shed 61.30 points to close at 13,456.26 after trading at a low of 13,422.10. Turnover was a vigorous HK$7.51 billion, in line with Monday's HK$7.38 billion. SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed lower in choppy trade on Tuesday after having spent most of the day confined to an eight point trading range. While softer metals prices ensured a shaky start to the day, the resource leaders quickly came off their lows. Afternoon strength in the banking sector ensured the day's losses were modest. The All Ordinaries index fell 5.0 points to 2,380.1.

JOHANNESBURG - Futures-related buying of South African shares helped industrial stocks retrace the bulk of their losses on Tuesday to end only a touch weaker. But gold shares were unable to shake the negative effects of bullion which fell to three-year lows in afternoon trade. Stocks shrugged off a weaker rand, dragging the gold index to its lowest close in 11 months.
At the close the industrial index was only 1.1 points softer at 7,991.7 after shares spent most of the day weak on offshore and local selling. The overall index ended 0.2 points softer at 6,699.5.
